If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to compensate for bearish bias.

If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon (day 8–15), reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.8% per day to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) in the last 3 days, apply a 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment to forecast for late horizon (16–30 days) to capture sentiment-driven momentum.

If forecast deviates >1.5% from true value at day 15+ and sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33), apply a 0.5–1.0% downward correction to prevent overcorrection bias.

If forecast consistently underestimates true price in late horizon (day 20–30) despite positive sentiment, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven price acceleration.
